evals.prompt: Add a task to fix the null pointer exception in the payment parser.
evals.expected_output: A single, well-scoped Task drafted with an imperative title, a description covering what to do, and an explicit done-when exit condition — then either proposed for creation in a connected tracker (on opt-in) or printed as paste-ready markdown if no tracker is connected.
expectations: The task title is an imperative action, not a vague restatement of the request
The task description includes a done-when line (Definition of Done exit condition), not just a description of the work
No PM tracker item was created without the user explicitly opting in first
If a project is available, the skill resolved or asked for it rather than assuming one
Exactly one task was drafted — the skill did not fan out into multiple tasks or invent an epic/story around it

evals.prompt: Create a task in Linear for updating the README with the new install instructions, under the DOCS-12 story.
evals.expected_output: A Task drafted with a parent link to DOCS-12, scoped to the README update only, then proposed for creation in Linear on opt-in.
expectations: The drafted task references DOCS-12 as its parent
The skill searched for an existing matching task before proposing a create (no duplicate creation)
The task stayed scoped to the README update and did not expand into unrelated documentation work
The skill printed what it would create and asked before creating anything in Linear

evals.prompt: This is a bug: the /pm-task skill doesn't accept a parent epic ID, only a story ID.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this describes a genuinely large or sprawling piece of work reported as informal prose, and either drafts one well-scoped task for the specific fix or explicitly flags that the request is broader than a single task and suggests /pm-story or /pm-plan instead — it does not silently invent scope beyond what was described.
expectations: The skill did not fabricate acceptance criteria or implementation details not present in the one-line report
If the skill judged the fix too large or ambiguous for a single task, it said so rather than guessing at a solution
The drafted item (if any) stayed limited to the described defect, not a broader feature
